easy.question: What are the three things food does for our body?
options: Gives energy, helps us grow, and protects from illness
Makes us tall, thin, and fast
Keeps us warm, cool, and sleepy
easy.answer: Gives energy, helps us grow, and protects from illness
easy.explanation: Food gives our body energy to work, helps us grow taller and stronger, and protects us from falling sick.

easy.question: Eating many different types of food every day is called a ______ diet.
easy.explanation: A balanced diet means eating many types of food -- grains, vegetables, fruits, pulses, dairy, and nuts -- so our body gets everything it needs.

easy.question: Which food group helps our muscles grow and repair?
options: Pulses and sprouts like moong and chana
easy.answer: Pulses and sprouts like moong and chana
easy.explanation: Pulses and sprouts are body-building foods that help our muscles grow and repair themselves.

easy.question: What happened when Aarav started eating a balanced diet?
easy.answer: Within two months, Aarav was bowling faster than ever. He felt more energetic and healthy because his body got all the nutrients it needed.
easy.explanation: Aarav earlier ate only rice and chips and felt tired. After eating grains, vegetables, fruits, dal, and milk, he became strong and fast.

easy.question: Which food group gives us energy to run, play, and study?
options: Grains like rice, roti, and millets
easy.answer: Grains like rice, roti, and millets
easy.explanation: Grains like rice, roti, idli, ragi, and jowar are energy foods that fuel all our daily activities.

medium.question: What is a balanced diet? Name the food groups that should be part of a healthy thali.
medium.answer: A balanced diet means eating many different types of food. A healthy thali should include grains for energy, vegetables for strength, fruits for vitamins, pulses for muscle growth, milk and dairy for strong bones, and nuts for healthy fats.
medium.explanation: A colourful thali with all food groups gives our body the energy, growth, and protection it needs.

medium.question: Which food group makes our bones and teeth strong?
medium.explanation: Milk, dahi, paneer, and chaas contain calcium which makes our bones and teeth strong.

medium.question: The more ______ on your plate, the healthier your meal.
medium.explanation: A colourful plate -- green palak, orange gajar, white rice, yellow dal, red tamatar -- means different nutrients for our body.

hard.question: Why did Aarav feel tired while playing cricket? What advice did the doctor give him? How did it help?
hard.answer: Aarav felt tired because he ate only plain rice and chips every day. His body was not getting all the nutrients it needed. The doctor told him his body was like a house built only with bricks -- no cement, doors, or windows. The doctor advised him to eat different grains like roti, idli, and millets, colourful vegetables, fresh fruits, pulses and sprouts, and milk and curd. Within two months of eating a balanced diet, Aarav became energetic and started bowling faster than ever. He told his friends that eating right was the secret to his speed.
hard.explanation: Eating only one or two types of food leaves our body incomplete. A balanced diet with different food groups gives us full strength and energy.

topics.topic: Where Does Our Food Come From?

easy.question: When we eat palak, which part of the plant are we eating?
easy.explanation: Palak (spinach) is the leaf of the palak plant. Other leaves we eat include methi, sarson, and pudina.

easy.question: Gajar, mooli, and chukandar are ______ of plants that we eat.
easy.explanation: Gajar (carrot), mooli (radish), and chukandar (beetroot) are roots of their plants.

easy.question: Honey is made by which creature?
easy.explanation: Honey bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey inside their hives.

easy.question: Name two foods that come from animals and two that come from plants.
easy.answer: From animals: milk (from cow or buffalo) and honey (from bees). From plants: rice (seeds of rice plant) and palak (leaves of palak plant).
easy.explanation: Most of our food comes from plants. Some foods like milk, ghee, honey, and eggs come from animals.

easy.question: Salt and water are two cooking ingredients that come from where?
easy.explanation: Salt comes from the sea or underground mines, and water comes from rivers, wells, and rain. Neither comes from a plant or an animal.

medium.question: We eat different parts of plants. Give one example of food from each: leaves, roots, stems, and seeds.
medium.answer: Leaves: palak. Roots: gajar. Stems: aloo. Seeds: chawal (rice).
medium.explanation: Plants give us food from many parts -- leaves (palak, methi), roots (gajar, mooli), stems (aloo, adrak), and seeds (rice, wheat, dal).

medium.question: Aloo (potato) is actually which part of the plant?
medium.explanation: Many people think potato is a root, but it is actually an underground stem called a tuber.

medium.question: Ghee and makhan are dairy products made from ______.
medium.explanation: Ghee and makhan (butter) are made from the cream of milk. All dairy products -- dahi, paneer, ghee, makhan -- come from milk.

hard.question: Most of our food comes from plants. Explain by giving examples of foods from different parts of plants.
hard.answer: Most of our food comes from plants, and we eat many different parts. Leaves -- we eat palak, methi, sarson, patta gobhi, pudina, and dhaniya. Fruits -- we eat tamatar, bhindi, shimla mirch, aam, and seb. Roots -- we eat gajar, mooli, chukandar, and shakarkandi. Stems -- aloo (underground stem), adrak, and pyaaz. Seeds as grains -- chawal, gehu, bajra, jowar, and ragi. Seeds as pulses -- moong, masoor, chana, and toor. We even eat flowers like kele ka phool. Plants truly give us an amazing variety of food.
hard.explanation: Plants are our main source of food. We eat almost every part of different plants -- leaves, fruits, roots, stems, seeds, and even flowers.

topics.name: Aarav Learns About Good Food

easy.question: Which of these is a fruit we enjoy in summer?
easy.explanation: Tarbooz (watermelon) is a summer fruit that cools our body. Other summer fruits include aam, kharbooja, and litchi.

easy.question: In winter, we eat gajar ka halwa and til ke laddu to keep our body ______.
easy.explanation: Winter foods like gajar ka halwa, til ke laddu, and sarson ka saag are rich and warm, helping our body stay warm from inside.

easy.question: Why should we not waste food?
easy.answer: We should not waste food because food is precious and many children in our country go to bed hungry. We should take only as much as we can finish and share with those who need it.
easy.explanation: Anna Daan (giving food) is one of the greatest acts of kindness in India. Wasting food while others go hungry is wrong.

easy.question: How many glasses of water should we drink every day?
easy.explanation: We should drink 6 to 8 glasses of water every day to keep our body working well and stay healthy.

medium.question: Why do we eat different foods in different seasons? Give examples for summer and winter.
medium.answer: We eat different foods because our body needs different things in different weather. In summer, we eat cooling foods like watermelon, nimbu shikanji, and cucumber raita to cool down and replace lost water. In winter, we eat warming foods like gajar ka halwa, sarson ka saag, and bajra roti to keep our body warm from inside.
medium.explanation: Our body is smart -- it craves cool foods when it is hot and warm foods when it is cold.

medium.question: Which refreshing drink is made from raw mango?
medium.explanation: Aam panna is a tangy and refreshing summer drink made from raw mango. It helps cool the body in hot weather.

hard.question: What are the different ways we can avoid wasting food? Why is sharing food important?
hard.answer: We can avoid wasting food by serving ourselves only as much as we can finish, not throwing away leftover rotis (we can give them to stray animals), eating home-cooked food which is healthier and less wasteful, and not throwing away fruits just because they have a small brown spot. Sharing food is important because many children in India go to bed hungry. When we share our tiffin with a friend who forgot theirs, we show kindness. In India, Anna Daan -- giving food -- is considered one of the greatest acts of goodness. A shared meal always tastes better than eating alone.
hard.explanation: Food is precious. Avoiding waste and sharing with others are important values that help both people and the environment.

hard.question: Why do people say 'paani hi jeevan hai' (water is life)? Name some healthy summer drinks.
hard.answer: People say 'paani hi jeevan hai' because our body cannot survive without water. Water makes up a large part of our body and is needed for everything from digesting food to keeping cool. In summer, we sweat a lot and lose water quickly, so we need to drink even more. Some healthy summer drinks include nariyal paani (tender coconut water), nimbu shikanji (lemon drink with salt and sugar), aam panna (raw mango drink), chaas (buttermilk), and ganne ka ras (sugarcane juice). These drinks replace the water we lose through sweat and keep our body cool and energized.
hard.explanation: Water is essential for life. We should drink at least 6-8 glasses daily, and healthy summer drinks help us stay hydrated.
